regulator: European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) and national competent authorities
rule_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 (MiCA), Article 7: marketing communications for crypto-assets other than ARTs and EMTs
summary: Marketing for crypto-assets other than ARTs and EMTs must be identifiable as marketing, fair, clear and not misleading, consistent with the white paper, and carry a statement that it was not approved by any authority. No marketing may run before a required white paper is published.
source_name: ESMA Interactive Single Rulebook, MiCA Article 7
notes: authorisation_required = Y because a white paper must be notified and published first; this is not a licence for the marketer itself. Title II applies from 2024-12-30.

regulator: European Banking Authority (EBA), ESMA and national competent authorities
rule_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 (MiCA), Article 29: marketing communications for asset-referenced tokens
summary: Issuers of asset-referenced tokens must publish marketing communications on their website and notify them to the competent authority on request. Authorities may not require prior approval before publication.
source_name: ESMA Interactive Single Rulebook, MiCA Article 29
notes: Title III applies from 2024-06-30. Content requirements in Art. 29(1) were not re-checked line by line for this release.

regulator: EBA, ESMA and national competent authorities
rule_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 (MiCA), Article 53: marketing communications for e-money tokens
summary: Marketing for e-money tokens must be consistent with the crypto-asset white paper and meet MiCA's marketing standards. Only authorised issuers may offer e-money tokens to the public.
source_name: ESMA Interactive Single Rulebook, MiCA Article 53
notes: Title IV applies from 2024-06-30.

regulator: National competent authorities (e.g. AFM, BaFin, AMF)
rule_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 (MiCA), Article 66: information and marketing duties of crypto-asset service providers
summary: Crypto-asset service providers must give clients fair, clear and not misleading information, make marketing identifiable as such, warn of risks of crypto-asset transactions and publish their fee policies.
notes: Article 66 content cross-checked against the Dutch AFM 2026 supervisory report (see NL-001). Only authorised CASPs may provide services in the EU after national transitional periods end.

rule_name: ESMA statement on CASPs offering unregulated services alongside MiCA-regulated services
summary: ESMA reminds crypto-asset service providers that offer both MiCA services and unregulated products not to confuse or mislead clients about which services carry MiCA protections.
notes: Supervisory statement; not a binding legal act.

rule_name: Kryptomärkteaufsichtsgesetz (KMAG), Crypto Markets Supervision Act, part of the FinmadiG
summary: Germany's national act that designates BaFin as MiCA competent authority and gives it supervisory and sanctioning powers. Marketing content rules come directly from MiCA.
notes: KMAG published in the Federal Law Gazette on 27 Dec 2024 (BGBl. 2024 I Nr. 438) with staged commencement; 30 Dec 2024 used as main date. No separate German crypto-advertising statute found.

regulator: Direction générale de la concurrence, de la consommation et de la répression des fraudes (DGCCRF); Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF)
rule_name: Loi n° 2023-451 du 9 juin 2023 visant à encadrer l'influence commerciale (influencer law)
summary: Paid influencers may not promote digital assets or token offerings unless the advertiser holds the required French registration or authorisation. Breaches can lead to administrative fines.
source_name: Ministère de l'Économie, Direction des affaires juridiques
notes: Published in the Journal officiel on 10 Jun 2023; exact commencement of each provision not re-checked, so effective_date left blank. Reference to PSAN status should be read alongside MiCA authorisation.

rule_name: Loi PACTE (Loi n° 2019-486) digital asset service provider (PSAN) regime: limits on direct solicitation, sponsorship and online advertising
summary: Under the PACTE regime, digital asset service providers without the optional AMF licence may not use direct solicitation (démarchage) or sponsorship, and online advertising is restricted under the consumer code.
notes: PSAN regime is being replaced by MiCA CASP authorisation; France's transitional period for PSANs is reported to have ended in mid-2026 (not verified). AMF doctrine on PSAN promotional communications updated 21 Dec 2022.

regulator: Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa (CONSOB); Banca d'Italia
rule_name: Decreto Legislativo 5 settembre 2024, n. 129 (MiCAR implementing decree)
summary: Italy's decree that names CONSOB and Banca d'Italia as MiCA competent authorities and sets their powers, sanctions and transition rules. Marketing content rules come from MiCA.
notes: Published in Gazzetta Ufficiale n. 215 of 13 Sep 2024; in force the next day. National VASP transition reported to have ended 30 Jun 2026 (secondary).

regulator: Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV)
rule_name: Circular 1/2022 de la CNMV sobre publicidad de criptoactivos presentados como objeto de inversión
summary: Spain's crypto advertising circular required prior notice to the CNMV for mass campaigns and set content standards. It was repealed by CNMV Circular 1/2024 once MiCA applied.
notes: Repealed by Circular 1/2024 of 17 Dec 2024 (BOE 27 Dec 2024, BOE-A-2024-27149). Crypto marketing in Spain now follows MiCA.

rule_name: AFM supervisory statements on crypto advertising under MiCAR (January 2025) and supervisory report on CASP marketing and cost disclosures (April 2026)
summary: The AFM supervises MiCA marketing rules and expects crypto ads to be clear and not misleading. Risk warnings must explain the actual risk rather than use a generic phrase, and terms such as 'savings' can mislead.
source_name: AFM, report on CASP marketing and cost disclosures (2026)
notes: effective_date reflects the January 2025 statement month; exact day not recorded. AFM has supervised MiCAR since 30 Dec 2024; transitional period ended 30 Jun 2025.

rule_name: S.I. No. 607/2024, European Union (Markets in Crypto-Assets) Regulations 2024
summary: Irish regulations that designate the Central Bank of Ireland as MiCA competent authority and set enforcement and transition rules. Marketing content rules come from MiCA.
notes: Notice published in Iris Oifigiúil on 12 Nov 2024. Transition for VASPs reported to have ended 30 Dec 2025 (secondary).

rule_name: Cryptoasset financial promotions regime: FSMA 2000 financial promotion restriction extended to qualifying cryptoassets, with FCA rules in PS23/6
summary: Crypto promotions to UK consumers must be made or approved by an authorised firm, by a registered cryptoasset business or under an exemption. They need a prescribed risk warning, a 24-hour cooling-off period for first-time investors, and no refer-a-friend or new-joiner bonuses.
source_name: FCA press release: tough new rules for marketing cryptoassets
notes: Applies to overseas firms marketing to UK consumers. Some technical features had until 8 Jan 2024. Influencer obligations covered in GB-002.

rule_name: FG24/1: Finalised guidance on financial promotions on social media
summary: Guidance on how financial promotion rules apply on social media, including to influencers who promote financial products. Unauthorised persons, including influencers, risk illegal promotion unless the content is approved.
notes: Replaces FG15/4. Does not create new rules; explains existing ones.

rule_name: Financial Services Act (FinSA/FIDLEG) Art. 68 and Financial Services Ordinance Art. 95: advertising for financial instruments
summary: Advertising for financial instruments must be clearly marked as advertising, refer to the prospectus and key information document, and match them. It applies to crypto tokens only where they qualify as financial instruments.
source_name: Federal Act on Financial Services, Art. 68 (bilingual reproduction)
notes: Text read from a bilingual reproduction, not the official Fedlex publication. Payment and utility tokens that are not financial instruments fall outside Art. 68; general unfair competition law still applies.

regulator: Federal Department of Finance / State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF); FINMA
rule_name: Draft amendment to the Financial Institutions Act creating crypto-institution and payment instrument institution licences (consultation 22 Oct 2025 to 6 Feb 2026)
summary: Proposed Swiss rules for crypto-based assets and stablecoins. The draft would require white papers and ads for certain unsupervised crypto issuers to state that the issuer is not FINMA-supervised and lacks the law's protections.
source_name: SIF factsheet on stablecoins and crypto-institutions
notes: SIF factsheet confirms the consultation; the advertising notice wording was read from a copy of the draft hosted by a law portal, not from an official source.

rule_name: Law No. 7518 amending Capital Markets Law No. 6362 (crypto asset service providers)
summary: Crypto asset service providers need CMB authorisation. Foreign platforms that target Turkish residents are treated as unauthorised providers.
source_name: Law No. 7518 (summary via CMS legal update)
notes: Published in Official Gazette No. 32590 on 2 Jul 2024. Primary Official Gazette text not checked for this release; an advertising-specific provision was not confirmed. CMB Communiqué III-35/B.1 applies from 13 Mar 2025 (secondary).

regulator: Bank of Russia; Federal Antimonopoly Service
rule_name: Amendments to the Federal Law on Advertising banning advertising of digital currency (2024)
summary: Reported 2024 amendments prohibit advertising of digital currencies and of goods or services meant to organise their circulation. Ad platforms such as Yandex updated their policies to block crypto exchange and mining ads.
source_name: Yandex Advertising news on new crypto advertising rules
notes: Only secondary sources checked (ad platform notice, crypto media). A 2026 digital currency law is also reported to keep a ban on advertising crypto payments. Official text not reviewed.

rule_name: Securities Act of 1933, Section 17(b) anti-touting provision
summary: Anyone paid to promote a security, including a crypto asset that is a security, must disclose the nature, source and amount of the payment. The SEC has settled several celebrity crypto cases on this basis.
notes: Applies only where the crypto asset is a security. Also see SEC 2017 statement on celebrity-backed ICOs. CFTC rules for commodity promotions were not researched for this release.

rule_name: Guides Concerning the Use of Endorsements and Testimonials in Advertising, 16 CFR Part 255 (2023 revision)
summary: Endorsers, including social media influencers, must clearly and conspicuously disclose material connections such as payment. The 2023 revision covers virtual influencers and social media tags. Applies to crypto ads like any other product.
notes: The Guides are administrative interpretations of Section 5 of the FTC Act, not binding rules on their own.

regulator: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), Federal Reserve, FDIC and state regulators
rule_name: GENIUS Act (Public Law 119-27), marketing provisions for payment stablecoins
summary: It is unlawful to market a product in the US as a payment stablecoin unless it is issued under the Act, or to claim a stablecoin is legal tender, federally insured or backed by the US government.
notes: Enacted 18 Jul 2025. Sec. 20: takes effect on the earlier of 18 months after enactment or 120 days after final implementing regulations. Whether final regulations have triggered the earlier date was not checked; review in 2027-Q1.

regulator: New York State Department of Financial Services (NYDFS)
rule_name: 23 NYCRR Part 200 (BitLicense), Section 200.18 Advertising and marketing
summary: Licensed virtual currency firms must keep all advertising for at least seven years, follow all federal and state disclosure rules in their ads, and must not run misleading marketing.
notes: Rule text read via a NYCRR reproduction (Justia/Cornell LII). Sub-national rule; applies to NYDFS licensees.

regulator: New York State Department of Financial Services (NYDFS)
rule_name: NYDFS guidance on virtual currency advertising and marketing (12 Nov 2026)
summary: Licensed virtual currency entities should make only accurate, evidence-based claims and give clear, prominent disclosures. They should have an ad review process and do due diligence on third-party promoters. Policies must be updated by 10 May 2027.
notes: risk_warning_required = Y reflects the clear disclosure expectation; the press release does not spell out a fixed risk warning text. Full guidance is on the DFS industry letters page.

regulator: Canadian Securities Administrators (CSA); Investment Industry Regulatory Organization of Canada (IIROC, now CIRO)
rule_name: Joint CSA/IIROC Staff Notice 21-330: Guidance for Crypto-Trading Platforms on advertising, marketing and social media use
summary: Crypto trading platforms that fall under securities law must keep advertising and social media content fair and not misleading. Regulators flagged gambling-style promotions as a concern.
source_name: CSA news release on Staff Notice 21-330
notes: Platforms operating while seeking registration file pre-registration undertakings (CSA Staff Notice 21-332, 22 Feb 2023).

rule_name: Circular 4/2019 on operations with virtual assets by credit institutions and fintech institutions
summary: Banks and licensed fintech institutions may use virtual assets only for internal operations and may not offer virtual asset services to the public. No crypto-specific advertising rule was found.
source_name: Banco de México, regulatory actions on virtual assets
notes: Banxico notes that companies other than these institutions are not barred by the circular from offering crypto services. Published in DOF 8 Mar 2019.

rule_name: Resoluções BCB nº 519, 520 e 521 de 2025 (virtual asset service providers, under Lei nº 14.478/2022)
summary: Brazil's central bank rules set authorisation and operating requirements for virtual asset service providers. Advertising-specific provisions were not confirmed for this release.
source_name: Banco Central do Brasil, Resolução BCB nº 520
notes: Published 10 Nov 2025; 2026-02-02 start date taken from a law firm summary. Need to check the resolution text for publicidade provisions.

rule_name: Resolución General CNV 994/2024: Registro de Proveedores de Servicios de Activos Virtuales (PSAV)
summary: Virtual asset service providers must register with the CNV. Foreign providers are treated as active in Argentina when they direct their offer or advertising to Argentine residents.
notes: In force from publication in the Boletín Oficial on 25 Mar 2024. Later CNV PSAV regulations were not reviewed for this release.

rule_name: Guidelines on Provision of Digital Payment Token Services to the Public (PS-G02)
summary: Crypto service providers should not market to the general public in Singapore, including in public areas, on public transport or through third parties such as social media influencers. They may promote only on their own websites, apps and official social media accounts.
notes: Also bars public crypto ATMs and promoting payment token derivatives as a safer alternative.

rule_name: Guidelines on Consumer Protection Safeguards by Digital Payment Token Service Providers (PS-G03)
summary: MAS expects crypto service providers to assess retail customers' risk awareness and not to offer them incentives to trade, or credit and leverage.
notes: Guidelines first issued 2 Apr 2024 and revised 19 Sep 2024; effective date reported as 4 Oct 2024 (secondary). Incentive restriction confirmed only in law firm summaries.

rule_name: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615), s.53ZRE: offence to issue advertisements for an unlicensed person's virtual asset service
summary: It is an offence to advertise a virtual asset service provided by an unlicensed person, or to actively market an unlicensed exchange to the Hong Kong public.
source_name: Hong Kong Government Gazette, AMLO amendment ordinance
notes: VATP licensing regime began 1 Jun 2023; non-contravention period ended 1 Jun 2024.

rule_name: Stablecoins Ordinance (Cap. 656)
summary: Issuing fiat-referenced stablecoins in Hong Kong needs an HKMA licence. Offering, and reportedly advertising, such stablecoins to retail investors is limited to licensed issuers and permitted offerors.
source_name: HKSAR Government press release, Stablecoins Ordinance commencement
notes: Commencement date confirmed from the government source. The advertising offence (reported as s.10) was confirmed only in secondary sources.

regulator: Financial Services Agency (FSA); Japan Virtual and Crypto assets Exchange Association (JVCEA)
rule_name: Payment Services Act amendments (Act No. 28 of 2019): advertising and solicitation rules for crypto-asset exchange services
summary: The 2019 amendments added advertising and solicitation rules for crypto-asset exchange services. Only FSA-registered exchanges may provide services, and the JVCEA adds self-regulatory advertising rules.
source_name: FSA, Working Group report on crypto-assets (Feb 2026)
notes: Main provisions reported in force from 1 May 2020 (secondary), so effective_date left blank. See JP-002 for the 2026 move to the FIEA.

rule_name: Act to Partially Amend the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act and the Payment Services Act (Act No. 64 of 2026)
summary: Moves crypto-asset regulation from the Payment Services Act to the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act, adding insider trading rules and stricter oversight. Securities-style sales and advertising conduct rules are expected to apply.
notes: Passed 15 Jul 2026, promulgated 23 Jul 2026 (secondary). Commencement date not confirmed from FSA; status may need updating.

regulator: Financial Services Commission (FSC); Financial Supervisory Service (FSS)
rule_name: Act on the Protection of Virtual Asset Users (Virtual Asset User Protection Act)
summary: The Act covers protection of user deposits and assets, unfair trading and FSC supervision of virtual asset service providers. No advertising-specific provision was found in FSC summaries.
notes: Only FSC English summaries checked. General endorsement and labelling rules from the Korea Fair Trade Commission may apply to paid promotions and were not reviewed.

rule_name: ASCI Guidelines for Advertising of Virtual Digital Assets and Linked Services
summary: Crypto and NFT ads must carry a prescribed disclaimer on risk and lack of regulation, may not compare VDAs to regulated products, and celebrities and influencers must do due diligence before endorsing.
notes: ASCI is a self-regulatory body, not a government regulator. Ads released before 1 Apr 2022 had until 15 Apr 2022 to comply.

rule_name: Information Sheet 269 (INFO 269): Discussing financial products and services online
summary: Explains how financial services law applies to social media influencers and to licensees who use them. Paid promotion of financial products can amount to unlicensed advice or dealing.
notes: Applies to crypto only where the product is a financial product; see AU-002.

regulator: Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC); Treasury
rule_name: Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework) Act 2026 (No. 38, 2026)
summary: Makes digital asset platforms and tokenised custody platforms financial products. Operators will need an Australian financial services licence, which brings them under financial services conduct and advertising law.
notes: Royal Assent 8 Apr 2026; commences 12 months later (secondary sources give 8 or 9 Apr 2027). Advertising consequences inferred, not confirmed in the Act text.

rule_name: SEC notifications on advertising by digital asset business operators (Notification GorThor 19/2565 and related SorThor notification)
summary: Digital asset operators' ads must be factual and balanced, carry prominent risk warnings in a set format, and be filed with the SEC before publication. Operators must report ad spending, including influencer use.
notes: Hearing paper describes advance filing at least 15 days before publication. 1 Sep 2022 start date taken from Thai news reporting of the SEC announcement. Influencer reporting point from news coverage.

rule_name: Proposed amendments to digital asset advertising rules (public hearing 02/2568)
summary: SEC proposal to change how risk warnings appear in digital asset ads, including font size alignment with securities rules and dropping the need for a continuous warning throughout an ad.
notes: Outcome of the 2025 hearing not checked; status may have changed.

rule_name: POJK No. 27 of 2024 on Trading of Digital Financial Assets including Crypto Assets (amended by POJK No. 23 of 2025)
summary: OJK took over crypto supervision from Bappebti and requires exchanges, clearing houses, custodians and traders to be licensed. Advertising-specific provisions were not confirmed for this release.
notes: Implementing circular SEOJK 20/2024 not reviewed for advertising content.

rule_name: SEC Memorandum Circulars No. 4 and No. 5, Series of 2025 (CASP Rules and CASP Guidelines)
summary: Crypto-asset service providers must register with the SEC. The rules also apply to anyone who offers, promotes or facilitates access to crypto services, including third parties paid to market them.
source_name: SEC Philippines advisory on unregistered crypto platforms (2025)
notes: Circulars dated 30 May 2025, effective 5 Jul 2025. Exposure draft s.7.2 barred promotion except by registered CASPs or authorised third parties; final wording not re-read.

regulator: Ministry of Finance (MOF); State Securities Commission
rule_name: Resolution No. 05/2025/NQ-CP on piloting the crypto asset market
summary: Five-year pilot of a regulated crypto market. Only organisations licensed by the Ministry of Finance may provide crypto services, including advertising and marketing them.
source_name: Baker McKenzie client alert on Resolution 05/2025
notes: Official government text not checked. Decree 284/2026/ND-CP on penalties reported 16 Jul 2026 (secondary).

rule_name: Guidelines on Advertising for Capital Market Products and Related Services (revised 2025)
summary: Prohibits advertising in Malaysia of services by persons not authorised by the SC, and makes advertisers responsible for marketing agents' compliance. Unregistered digital asset exchanges are a stated enforcement focus.
notes: Revised version released 27 Mar 2025; effective date not stated in the release. Application to digital assets assumes they are capital market products. SC worked with Google to restrict unregistered exchange ads from 14 Apr 2026 (secondary).

regulator: People's Bank of China (PBOC); China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) and other agencies
rule_name: Notice on Further Preventing and Dealing with Virtual Currency and Other Related Risks (Yin Fa [2026] No. 42)
summary: Mainland China keeps treating virtual currency business as illegal financial activity, bars offshore firms from serving domestic users, restricts offshore yuan stablecoins and sets a first framework for real-world asset tokens.
notes: Reported to replace the 2021 notice (CN-002). PBOC primary text not checked for this release. authorisation_required = N because no licence path exists.

regulator: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and nine other agencies
rule_name: Notice on Further Preventing and Disposing of Risks of Speculation in Virtual Currency Trading (Yin Fa [2021] No. 237)
summary: Declared virtual currency business activities illegal, including services by offshore exchanges to mainland residents, and called for tighter control of related online content.
notes: Dated 15 Sep 2021, published 24 Sep 2021. Repeal by the 2026 notice confirmed only in secondary sources.

rule_name: Guiding Principles for the Management of Virtual Asset Service Providers
summary: Foreign virtual asset platforms that have not registered and filed anti-money laundering compliance in Taiwan may not solicit business there. Domestic providers must keep advertising and solicitation fair and honest.
source_name: The Block report on FSC guidelines
notes: FSC primary text not checked. Amended AML Act requiring VASP registration reported to take effect end of 2024 (secondary).

rule_name: Virtual Assets Act, 2026
summary: Any person offering virtual asset services in or from Pakistan needs a PVARA licence; unlicensed activity carries fines and possible imprisonment. Advertising-specific provisions were not confirmed.
source_name: National Assembly of Pakistan, Virtual Assets Bill as passed
notes: Passed by Parliament in March 2026 (secondary); bill states it comes into force at once. Replaced the Virtual Assets Ordinance 2025.

rule_name: Regulations on the Marketing of Virtual Assets and Related Activities 2024
summary: Apply to all marketing of virtual assets in or targeting the UAE, whether or not the marketer is licensed by VARA. They replace VARA's 2022 marketing orders.
notes: A limited exemption for unlicensed firms at physical events in Dubai and duties for third-party marketing agencies reported in secondary sources. VARA jurisdiction excludes DIFC.

jurisdiction: United Arab Emirates: Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM)
rule_name: FSRA Conduct of Business Rulebook (COBS) Chapter 3 financial promotion rules as applied to Virtual Assets (COBS 17), and Guidance on Regulation of Virtual Asset Activities in ADGM
summary: In ADGM, conduct rules for financial promotions also cover virtual assets, and only FSRA-accepted virtual assets may be used by authorised firms.
source_name: ADGM FSRA Guidance, Regulation of Virtual Asset Activities in ADGM
notes: Guidance version dated 10 Jun 2025 checked. Free zone rule; applies within ADGM only.

regulator: Capital Markets Authority (formerly Securities and Commodities Authority, SCA)
rule_name: CMA Decision No. 4/R.M/2026 on virtual asset activities and service providers
summary: New federal framework for licensed virtual asset activities, issued after SCA was reconstituted as the Capital Markets Authority on 1 Jan 2026. Advertising provisions were not confirmed.
notes: Replaces earlier SCA rules (Cabinet Resolution 111/2022, SCA Decision 26/2023) according to secondary sources. Primary text not checked.

regulator: Saudi Central Bank (SAMA); Capital Market Authority (CMA)
rule_name: Standing committee warnings that virtual currencies are not regulated in the Kingdom and no party is licensed to deal in them
summary: Saudi authorities state that no party is licensed to deal in virtual currencies. A permanent committee works with other agencies to curb marketing of unlicensed forex and digital currency schemes, including paid influencer ads.
notes: Official warning, not a statute. Later SAMA notice describes influencer-driven ads for unlicensed schemes. authorisation_required = N because no licence path exists.

regulator: Capital Market, Insurance and Savings Authority (CMISA); Israel Securities Authority (ISA)
rule_name: Supervision of Financial Services (Regulated Financial Services) Law, 2016: licensing of financial asset service providers including virtual currency
summary: Providers of financial services in virtual currencies need a CMISA licence. A crypto-specific advertising rule was not confirmed for this release.
notes: ISA published a draft directive under the Investment Advice and Marketing Law on 5 Aug 2026 (secondary); relevance to crypto ads not checked.

rule_name: QCB Circular No. 6 of 2018 (bitcoin trading) and Circular No. 46 of 2019 (virtual assets and VASPs)
summary: Qatar's central bank treats crypto trading as illegal and does not license virtual asset services onshore, so no lawful channel exists to promote them.
source_name: Al Tamimi & Co update on QCB warning
notes: QCB primary circulars not checked. The QFC Digital Assets Framework 2024 covers tokenisation inside the QFC and is not included here.

rule_name: Amendments to the SEC Rules on Digital Assets Issuance, Offering Platforms, Exchange and Custody (2024), including advertisement, marketing and promotion
summary: Nigeria's SEC added rules on advertising, marketing and promotion of digital assets, aimed partly at social media finfluencers. Digital asset platforms must be registered with the SEC.
source_name: SEC Nigeria, re-exposure of amendments to digital asset rules
notes: Exact commencement not confirmed, so effective_date left blank. Investments and Securities Act 2025 (commenced 25 Mar 2025) treats digital assets as securities.

rule_name: Proposed Rules on Digital and Virtual Assets Operations, Custody and Markets
summary: Proposed SEC rules covering issuance, offering, trading and custody of digital and virtual assets under the Investments and Securities Act 2025.
source_name: SEC Nigeria, proposed rules page (published 20 Aug 2026)
notes: Advertising content of the proposal not reviewed in detail.

rule_name: Declaration of crypto assets as a financial product under the FAIS Act (General Notice 1350 of 2022)
summary: Crypto assets are financial products under the FAIS Act, so anyone giving advice or intermediary services on them needs an FSCA licence and must follow FAIS conduct rules.
notes: Advertising specifics in the FAIS General Code of Conduct were not re-read for this release.

regulator: Capital Markets Authority (CMA); Central Bank of Kenya (CBK)
rule_name: Virtual Asset Service Providers Act, 2025 (Act No. 20 of 2025)
summary: Kenya's first licensing law for virtual asset service providers. When the Act commenced, regulators said no VASP had yet been licensed under it.
source_name: Kenya Law, Virtual Asset Service Providers Act
notes: Assented 15 Oct 2025, gazetted 21 Oct 2025. Advertising rules are in KE-002.

regulator: National Treasury; Capital Markets Authority (CMA); Central Bank of Kenya (CBK)
rule_name: Virtual Asset Service Providers Regulations, 2026
summary: Regulations under the VASP Act that reportedly set rules for advertising and promotion of virtual assets, including risk disclosures and limits on misleading online marketing.
notes: Published 22 Jul 2026 according to the secondary source. Kenya Gazette text not checked.
